N-cone.objects: Real Banach spaces A0,A1, a continuous injective inclusion and a nonnegative cone M+ with a positive definite, degree-one gauge.
N-cone.domain: Finite (0,T), 1 <= p,q <= infinity, restricted to q>1 or to q=1 with p finite.
N-cone.fixed_and_variable: The cone, gauge, inclusion, constants and exponents are fixed; v varies through the one uniformly bounded family F.
N-cone.hypotheses: Only nonnegative scaling closure is assumed. Gauge domination and sequential compactness in A0 are explicit, as are strong measurability, almost-everywhere cone membership, measurable gauge and the A1-valued distributional derivative bound.
N-cone.equations: The degree-one identity [cz]=c[z], A0 domination and joint family bound are complete. The later two-point estimate uses [u]+[v], never [u-v].
N-cone.quantifiers: Every gauge-bounded sequence has an A0-convergent subsequence. One bound controls all trajectories; the excluded (infinity,1) pair is stated exactly.
N-cone.conclusion: Relative compactness in Lp(A0). The manuscript proves continuous A0 representatives in the infinity case and makes no claim that limits lie in a nonclosed cone.
N-cone.status: Established Barrett-Suli source result. The local weak-space construction avoids a specifically recorded proof gap without claiming the source theorem false.
N-cone.local_definitions: All gauge properties used by normalization occur in the statement. Addition, subtraction closure and a gauge triangle inequality are not assumed.

N-maitre.objects: Banach spaces E1,E2, a fixed map K, the input family U and image family V={K(u):u in U}. The conclusion concerns V.
N-maitre.domain: The same finite time interval; target 1 <= p <= infinity and a possibly different auxiliary 1 < r <= infinity.
N-maitre.fixed_and_variable: K and the spaces are fixed. u varies through U, v=K(u) varies through V; one r and its bound serve the whole family.
N-maitre.hypotheses: Bounded sets have relatively compact K-images; U is L1-bounded; the compositions are strongly measurable; V is contained in Lp, Lr-bounded and uniformly translation-continuous in target Lp(E2).
N-maitre.equations: The Lr bound and target-Lp translation limit are preserved. The derived tail keeps (CU/M)^(1-1/r) CV and (CU/M)||K(0)|| separately.
N-maitre.quantifiers: Existence of one r>1 is not identified with p. Measurability is assumed, not deduced from an unstated continuity of K.
N-maitre.conclusion: Image compactness in Lp(E2), with continuous representatives and C compactness at infinity; no recovery of input compactness.
N-maitre.status: Established published source result; the explicit r=infinity consequence is valid on a finite interval. The finite-net averaging proof is identified as local reconstruction.
N-maitre.local_definitions: Map compactness is written as the bounded-set image property. No injectivity, linearity or monotonicity is inserted.

N-simon.objects: The fixed Banach triple X, B, Y and one family F; X compactly injects into B, which continuously injects into Y.
N-simon.domain: One finite interval (0,T); all 1 <= p <= infinity. Translation norms use the shortened interval (0,T-h).
N-simon.fixed_and_variable: T, p, spaces and embeddings stay fixed while f varies in F and h decreases to zero.
N-simon.hypotheses: A family-uniform Lp(X) bound and family-uniform Lp(Y) translation limit are both retained in the displayed canonical statement.
N-simon.equations: The two displayed family conditions are unchanged; the proof later uses the same p in the weak Cauchy norm and strong norm upgrade.
N-simon.quantifiers: The supremum over F lies inside the h-limit. The later Ehrling eta is chosen before the Cauchy indices, not separately for each pair.
N-simon.conclusion: Relative compactness in Lp(B) for finite p; relative compactness of the continuous B representatives in C([0,T];B) at infinity.
N-simon.status: Established source-derived theorem, presented as a representative form of Simon Theorem 5, not as an original contribution.
N-simon.local_definitions: The compact-injection notation, relative compactness, translation domain and continuous representative convention are supplied before use.

fast_route_reconstruction.finding: On a fresh pass I reconstructed: linear bound -> compact integrals in Y -> criterion -> Ehrling in B; input truncation -> compact E2 values -> hull averages -> criterion in E2; gauge truncation -> criterion in A1 -> two-point upgrade in A0. The opening map and final table expose this path without hiding the later slow steps.

slow_step_reproduction.finding: I reproduced the two slow constructions: replace compact-valued trajectories by measurable nearest-net simple functions to place averages in a compact closed hull; normalize two cone points by the sum of their gauges and use a common convergent subsequence plus injectivity. I also recomputed K1 and the exact 1/[n(p+1)] ramp error.

condition_transfer.finding: The homogeneous test passes only after alpha*p>=1, measurable inverse lifts, compactness of K on bounded sets, and equality of derivative and output spaces are checked. Outside that interface the manuscript retains distinct unknowns and topologies; it never passes a weak-space derivative to Maitre in a stronger space.

Obtain compact interval integrals from t.finding: Holder bounds each interval integral by |I|^(1-1/p) MX in X. Compact X-to-B and continuous B-to-Y inclusions make the integrals compact in Y; the stated uniform translations then meet the imported criterion in Y.

Choose the Ehrling parameter before the.finding: The normalized contradiction proves Ehrling using compactness and injectivity. The displayed upgrade has 2 eta MX plus C_eta times the weak Cauchy norm. Eta is fixed below epsilon/(4MX) before indices; MX=0 is separated. The dense full-measure argument also constructs the continuous B representative at infinity.

Bound the exceptional-set measure and th.finding: Markov gives |G_M| <= CU/M. v_M equals v or K(0), hence is measurable. Holder gives the uniform L1 tail including K(0); its vanishing uses r>1. Only L1 error is consumed for interval integrals, so no invalid p<=r assumption is needed.

Prove compactness of the closed convex h.finding: The finite delta-net replaces every convex combination by one in a fixed finite simplex. Total boundedness plus completeness makes the closed hull compact. First-nearest-net cells are measurable, and their normalized measures give the integral as a limit of convex combinations.

Transfer compactness to untruncated inte.finding: M is chosen from the uniform tail before a finite net for the truncated integrals. This proves total boundedness of the original integrals in E2. The criterion then uses the independently assumed target-Lp translations, including its continuous-representative endpoint.

Derive a uniform supremum bound from W11.finding: Choose a time with norm below the mean plus epsilon, integrate v-prime, then let epsilon decrease. This proves the exact supremum bound T^(-1)||v||L1+||v-prime||L1, rather than assuming an independent amplitude estimate.

Use Fubini and bounded-amplitude interpo.finding: Fubini counts each derivative value for at most h units of time, giving hD in L1. The pointwise difference is bounded by 2K0, so the p-th power is at most (2K0)^(p-1)hD. Taking the root gives h^(1/p), not h, for arbitrary finite p.

Use Holder for a supremum translation mo.finding: Holder on each interval (t,t+h) gives h^(1-1/q)||v-prime||Lq. The text explicitly treats q=infinity and the nonvanishing exponent-zero bound at q=1; it does not use that bound to assert supremum compactness.

Compute the ramp derivative bound and fi.finding: The ramp has height one, derivative n on an interval of length 1/n, hence derivative L1 norm one. Direct integration gives ||v_n-w||p^p=1/[n(p+1)] for finite p; every bound and the pointwise step limit was recalculated.

Prove lack of L-infinity compactness fro.finding: A uniform limit of these continuous ramps would be continuous, while every subsequence has the discontinuous step as pointwise limit. For continuous differences the essential supremum equals the supremum, so an L-infinity Cauchy subsequence would give exactly that impossible uniform limit.

Calculate the pairwise L1 separation of.finding: For m>n each n-cell contains an even number of alternating m-cells. The signs differ on half the interval, so every L1 distance is one. Squaring gives the constant image one with zero translations. This disproves input recovery, not Maitre image compactness.

Normalize both cone points by the sum of.finding: Failure at eta0 gives a positive sum of gauges a_n. Dividing both points by a_n keeps them inside the cone with gauges at most one. Compactness gives two A0 limits; their A1 difference tends to zero because it is bounded by n^(-1) times a bounded A0 difference. Injectivity contradicts A0 separation above eta0.

Derive the A1 supremum bound and control.finding: Holder and gauge domination give L1(A1)<=C1 C0 T^(1-1/p)G. W11 gives K1=C1 C0 T^(-1/p)G+T^(1-1/q)D. The gauge bad set has measure at most T^(1-1/p)G/R, so the A1 L1 tail is bounded by K1 times that quantity.

Obtain compact interval integrals and ap.finding: Gauge-bounded values have compact closure in A0 and hence A1. The already proved compact-hull construction and uniform tail give compact integrals in A1. q=1 uses the finite-p Fubini-amplitude estimate; q>1 uses Holder. The criterion therefore applies in every allowed case.

Upgrade weak-space Cauchy convergence wi.finding: Two-point Ehrling plus Minkowski produces 2 eta G plus the weak Cauchy term. Eta precedes the indices, and G=0 is separate. At p=infinity, the full-measure bounded-gauge set and continuous A1 representative give a continuous A0 extension. The cited source-gap concern is scoped separately.

Construct the degree-one inverse gauge a.finding: Injectivity and positive homogeneity imply K(0)=0 and inverse scaling c^(1/alpha). The inverse gauge therefore has degree one. Boundedness of the compact unit-ball image gives ||K(x)||<=C||x||^alpha, and gauge-bounded sets arise from bounded preimages, proving the needed compact embedding.

Compute the inverse-lift L1 bound and th.finding: Since alpha*p>=1, Holder gives the explicit inverse-lift L1 bound T^(1-1/(alpha*p))G^(1/alpha), with T at p=infinity. Strongly measurable lifts are an assumption. Gauge and same-space derivative bounds give W11(E2), then an amplitude bound and every fixed finite Lr bound.

Check matching derivative and output spa.finding: The derivative is measured in E2 itself, so the derived translations satisfy Maitre in that same target space. q>1 permits target infinity and yields C compactness. Arbitrary weak derivative spaces or arbitrary cones do not satisfy this change-of-variables argument; that noncoverage is not a counterexample to other methods.
